c1_call.text: I'll call Kenneth's line when I get home.

c1_sign.text: ALL MAY TAKE REFUGE IN THE RED COUNTY COMMUNAL CHAPEL
Someone painted these tonight. The paint's still running.

c1_turn.text: Town's that way. Addie's that way.
...If anybody knows what's happening, it's whoever painted those.
Just for a minute. Then Addie.

c1_bounds.text: I don't need to go this way.

c1_arrive.text: Lights on at Louis's. Okay. Everything's fine.

c1_figure_wait.text: Are you hurt? Do you need help?

c1_inside.text: That was Louis. That was Louis's face.

c1_lockbox_open.text: Okay. You hope you never need it.

c1_lockbox_wrong.text: No. Think. Addie's birthday. Month, then day.

c1_lockbox_noclue.text: Three numbers. I always use the same three... Addie's birthday. It's on the kitchen calendar, in her crayon.

c1_window_scratch.text: The bedroom window. He's at the bedroom window.

c1_wardrobe_done.text: That'll hold. That has to hold.

c1_body.text: It's still smoking. Why is it still smoking?

c1_body_look.text: Under the burned skin, the cardigan he wore every Sunday. His glasses, bent into his face.

c1_broadcast.text: THIS IS AN EMERGENCY ALERT FOR THE CITY OF KENNEDY AND SURROUNDING AREAS.
AT APPROXIMATELY 7:40 P.M. A WIDESPREAD EVENT OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN WAS REPORTED WITHIN THE CITY OF KENNEDY.
RESIDENTS ARE ADVISED TO REMAIN INDOORS. LOCK ALL DOORS AND WINDOWS.
DO NOT APPROACH PERSONS WHO APPEAR INJURED OR DISORIENTED.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO TRAVEL. ROADS INTO KENNEDY ARE CLOSED.
FURTHER INFORMATION WILL BE PROVIDED AS IT BECOMES AVAILABLE.

c1_landline.text: Okay. I'm coming to get you.

c1_car_wrecked.text: The windshield is caved in. The hood is torn up, and the front tyre is shredded.
His truck. He kept it running.

c1_truck_locked.text: An old pickup, more rust than paint. Locked.
He never left the keys in it. They'll be in the house.

c1_louis_door.text: The door is split down the middle, one half still swinging from the top hinge.

c1_photo_school.text: Her first day of kindergarten. Kenneth took it. She made me promise not to cry at the door. I lied.

c1_photo_lake.text: Kenneth and Addie at Lake Ruth, both squinting into the sun like the same person, forty years apart.

c1_photo_birthday.text: Addie's birthday. She blew the candles out twice, because the first time "didn't count."

c1_photo_christmas.text: Christmas morning. Addie was up at five, which meant I was up at five.

c1_calendar.text: Addie's week circled in red. Next Monday.
Flipped back to June: the 12th circled in pink, in Addie's own crayon. "MY BIRTHDAY!!"

c1_fridge.text: Addie's drawing. A purple cat with a very long tail: "PICKLE."

c1_addie_bed.text: Addie's bed, made the way she likes it, with Pickle on the pillow.

c1_journal.text: Oct 14. Addie's week starts Monday. I bought the cereal with the marshmallows even though I swore I wouldn't.
She's decided the cat on her backpack is called "Pickle." I've been informed this is final.
Work was the usual. Sergeant Dale lost his reading glasses on his own head again. Somebody called in a cow on the county road. Twice.
Louis finished the porch step. Addie "helped." She has her own hammer now, God help us. He wouldn't take money, so he went home with the rest of the lasagna.
He says the tulips go in next month, and Addie's in charge of the bulbs.
Note to self: the lockbox code is still Addie's birthday. Change it. (I won't.)

c1_bible_journal.text: For Rose. Eleven years tomorrow. Some mornings I still set out two cups before I remember.
Lord, keep the girls next door. The little one asks me a hundred questions about the saints and remembers every answer. Her mother works too hard and won't sit down.
Father Abel asked about the truck again. I told him I'll drive it once more, to the chapel for Christmas Eve. The keys stay in the safe until then. Rose's verse keeps them: John 3:16.
Oct 21. My back burns. There is a mark there I can't see in the mirror. I hear something under my own voice. I've locked the doors.
If I am not myself, Lord, let them be far away.

c1_bible_found.text: A small leather journal in the drawer. Louis's handwriting.

c1_rosary.text: Louis's rosary, tucked behind the toilet tank like it was hidden in a hurry. A paper tag on the cord: "Rose's. For keeping."

c1_rose_photo.text: Louis and Rose outside the chapel. He kept it by the door, so she'd be the first thing he saw coming home.
I only met her twice. She called me "the new girl" for three years.

c1_grave.text: A little wooden cross in the flower bed, hand-carved: ROSE.

c1_well.text: The old well. Louis kept a board over it for Addie's sake.

c1_l_wardrobe.text: His coats, still smelling of pipe smoke. In a pocket: a battery, half used.

c1_desk_empty.text: Pencils, a magnifying glass, his reading glasses' case. Empty.

c1_l_bed.text: The sheets are torn apart from the inside. The tears are scorched brown at the edges.

c1_l_window.text: Rain blows in across the sill. Wet footprints cross the floor to the window. Bare feet.

c1_fridge_meds.text: Behind the milk, pills in an orange bottle. A few left.

c1_fridge_empty.text: Milk, butter, a covered dish. Nothing she needs.

c1_l_safe_open.text: Inside: a ring of keys on a red fob, and a photo.

c1_med_full.text: She's not hurt enough to need them.

c1_heal.text: She dry-swallows two of the pills.

c1_storm_photo.text: Me and Louis fixing up his porch after that storm, all those years back. A branch took out the post and half the rail.
He wouldn't let me pay for the lumber, so I paid him in coffee. He still says I owe him.

c1_step_photo.text: Louis and Addie, the day they fixed my porch step. She wouldn't put that hammer down for a week.
On the border, in his handwriting: "Step fixed! Head carpenter: Addie."

c1_radio.text: ...the Red County Sheriff's office is asking folks to check on their neighbors tonight. We've had a number of missing persons reports come in since this afternoon.
Three more in the last hour. Two out along the county road, one in Kennedy proper. A woman who went out to get her mail and didn't come back in.
If you have any information, call the Sheriff's office. And, folks... lock your doors tonight.

c1_gone.text: Where he lay, only a dark smear. It drags across the floor toward the bedroom, and the broken window.
He was dead. I watched him go down. He was dead.

c1_stalk_reveal.text: I shot you. I watched you go down.

c1_stalk_down.text: Stay down. Please, Louis. Just stay down.

c1_up_crash.text: The truck. Get to the truck!

c1_louis_killed.text: Something glints beside him. A thin gold chain, snapped, and a ring on it.

c1_l_window_back.text: Glass and rain across the floor. Wet footprints go out over the sill, and come back in.
